warrant: The observable is every cell of every prognostic field in the final state dump, compared as |c - r| <= 1e-10 + 1e-08|r|; the relative part is the working bound because the graded fields span many orders of magnitude, the absolute part covers cells at or near zero. The graded observable is the whole final dump (U, V, W, T, S, Eta, PH) plus the five time-averaged diagnostics streams that fall exactly on the end of the window, compared pointwise, and the reason the round-off bound is achievable here is much stronger than for the spun-up AIM decks: the run begins from an exactly uniform, motionless, completely DRY state (theta=tRef by level, specific humidity zero everywhere, no pickup), so over the first steps there is no convection to trigger (phy_convmf.F gates on a boundary-layer humidity threshold that a dry column never crosses), no large-scale condensation (phy_lscond.F gates on relative humidity above RHLSC), and no ice (thsice starts with iceMask=0 because startIceModel=0 with nIter0=0 and no thSIce*_InitFile takes the no-pickup branch of thsice_ini_vars.F). The switch-flipping argument that the other AIM checks have to make probabilistically is therefore nearly vacuous here for the first several steps: what the window measures is the radiative heating, the surface fluxes over land, ocean and the slab mixed layer, and the geostrophic adjustment of the atmosphere to real topography, all of which are smooth functions of the state. The remaining floors are ordinary: cg2d converges on cg2dTargetResWunit=7.8E-16 so an iteration-count difference perturbs Eta at about 1e-15, the rStar rescaling divides by column thicknesses bounded by hFacMin=0.2 over topography that is fixed, and the Shapiro filter is a fixed stencil with no limiter. The variant perturbs SOLC, the area-averaged solar constant of pkg/aim_v23 (package default 342. W/m2, set in phy_const.h by INPHYS before AIM_READPARMS reads the present-but-empty AIM_PAR_FOR group of data.aimphys); phy_driver.F passes it to SOL_OZ on every step and the top-of-atmosphere insolation FSOL is directly proportional to it, so the perturbation enters the shortwave heating of every daylit column on the very first step. A REVIEWER MUST KNOW WHY ABLWV1 WAS NOT USED HERE even though it is the variant of the sibling aim.5l_cs check: ABLWV1 enters RADLW only through TAU2 = EXP(-DELTAP*ABLWV1*QA), and QA (specific humidity) is identically zero at nIter0=0 in this deck, so a perturbation of ABLWV1 would have literally no effect on the first step and would only creep in from the lowest model level once surface evaporation has moistened it; SOLC has no such degeneracy. Faults: This is the only check that reaches pkg/thsice's surface energy balance under an atmospheric model. Getting the ice/ocean flux split wrong in phy_suflux_post.F when aim_splitSIOsFx is on, or solving the ice surface temperature explicitly instead of by the Newton iteration of thsice_solve4temp.F, changes the surface sensible and latent fluxes by several W/m2 and the lowest-level T by parts in 1e-5 per step. Dropping the mixed-layer heat capacity term or the relaxation in thsice_slab_ocean.F changes the sea surface temperature by parts in 1e-6 per step, which the surface fluxes carry into T. On the atmospheric side the same faults as the primary AIM check apply: a dropped longwave band in RADLW, a cheapened mass-flux closure in phy_convmf.F, a fixed drag replacing the stability-corrected surface flux. Because this deck starts from rest and dry, the radiative and surface-flux faults dominate the window while the convective ones barely show - which is exactly complementary to the spun-up primary deck. The expensive path under test is pkg/aim_v23's aim_do_physics.F/phy_driver.F over 6144 columns each step (phy_shtorh.F, phy_convmf.F, phy_lscond.F, the SOL_OZ/RADSW shortwave and the four-band RADLW longwave of phy_radiat.F, the surface-flux chain phy_suflux_prep/land/ocean/sice/post.F with aim_splitSIOsFx separating the sea-ice and open-ocean fluxes, phy_vdifsc.F); pkg/thsice's thsice_step_temp.F, thsice_solve4temp.F and thsice_slab_ocean.F over every ocean column; pkg/land's implicit ground-temperature solve; and on the dynamics side mom_vecinv.F with the experiment's own mom_vi_hfacz_diss.F and mom_vi_mask_vort3.F, the rStar update, gad_advection for T and q, and shap_filt_uv_s2.F/shap_filt_tracer_s2.F over the exch2 halos.. The nominal-versus-variant spread recorded by selfcheck is the measurement of the round-off amplification under this exact rule, and the bound is finalised against it with the human.
